utterances.text: For the record the second name mentioned was Bjelovac because it doesn't show up in the transcript either. So I think we can proceed now.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber which company of the deserters from Jahorina travelled to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: The 1st Company.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did their company commander travel with them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: Yes, I think he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And that was Mr. Djuric; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you describe the uniforms that the Jahorina members were wearing?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Judge Kwon and myself are thinking of the same thing at the same time. Mr. Thayer, I need your guidance here. Lines 12 to 16 and possibly even 17 and 18, do you think it's safe to keep them in open session or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do. I recognise it's -- it's a -- something of a tight-rope. The vast, vast majority of the testimony would be in private session if we were to continue on -- on that line. I recognise the ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. If you think it's safe, let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: It's okay. I have given thought to it, and I think we can err on this side. Thank you for the intervention.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, can you describe the uniforms worn by the Jahorina members?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: Well, they had camouflage uniforms that were different from those worn by the other members of the special police brigade and of the police. It was camouflage, I can't really describe the colours to you, but it was different from the special police brigade members.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I believe that the witness said, "two-piece uniform," which I cannot find in transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Do you confirm that, Witness? Did you say a two-piece uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I remember, yes, it was a two-piece uniform.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Still camouflage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Just to be clear, the two-piece uniform you recall being worn by the Jahorina members, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: As far as I remember, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And the regular special police brigade members, as opposed to the Jahorina members, do you recall what types of uniforms they wore?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: Well, the regular special police brigade members had boiler suits and they also had camouflage uniforms, but of a different colour.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And by boiler suits, we're talking about cover-alls or overalls; is that correct? A one-piece suit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: Yes, it was a one-piece suit. We use this term, kombinezon, overalls, but the special brigade also had some two-piece uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: What type of weapons were the Jahorina members carrying, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: Well, members of the Jahorina unit carried only automatic rifles. They did not have any side arms, and they had some protective equipment, bullet-proof vests that were blue. I think they were made in Israel. They did not have -- they only had Kevlar plates, not armoured plates.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did the Jahorina unit have any armoured vehicles or tanks or any of that type of equipment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And how about other detachments of the special police brigade, did they have tanks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: Some units did have tanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall which units had tanks, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: The 2nd detachment from Sekovici had tanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did any of the units have what are sometimes referred to as a BOV or three-barreled armoured vehicle, combat vehicle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall which detachments had those vehicles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: Well, as far as I remember, the Sekovici unit had them. I don't know if there were any other units that have them -- that had them, I don't know which ones had them, but quite a few units did.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And back to the uniforms again, just for a second. Did the Jahorina uniforms have any insignia on them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: They did not have any insignia. Or rather they did not have any insignia on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And how about the regular special police brigade members, did they have insignia or patches on their uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: The special police brigade had their insignia, worn on the sleeve.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, I want to focus, or refocus your attention back to Bratunac on 11 July 1995, after you arrived and were accommodated. Did you meet at some point with Mr. Borovcanin that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: As far as I remember, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you tell the Trial Chamber what occurred at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: Well, I was told that I should do a reconnaissance of the Potocari area, the UNPROFOR base and also the access leading towards Srebrenica, and after completing this reconnaissance mission I was to report to him. I took some of the officers with me, and I think that we had a local police officer with us. We did the reconnaissance, and I reported to Mr. Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you remember approximately what time of the day it was when you conducted this reconnaissance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: I think it was just before dusk, so just before nightfall.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what did you report back to Mr. Borovcanin that you saw, if anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: Well, I reported to him that in the UNPROFOR base area there were civilians gathering there, that there were quite a few of them, and this was the gist of my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what, if anything, did Mr. Borovcanin tell you at that point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: Well, as far as I know, that I should await further orders and that I should go back to the base where we were quartered, and that I should await further orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did he tell you about any meeting that was underway at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: I think it was in the evening, I don't know the exact time. He told me that in Bratunac, I think maybe in the hotel, that there was a meeting between the UNPROFOR commander, representatives of the Muslim people and General Mladic, and that the fate was decided there, that they -- that the civilians were to be evacuated from the Potocari area. And I was also told that the representative of the Muslims had signed, had allegedly signed these documents about the evacuation of the civilians from the Potocari area.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: In addition to telling you this information concerning the results of the meeting, sir, did Mr. Borovcanin issue you any further orders that evening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: He told me that in the morning we were supposed to go into the Potocari area and to secure UNPROFOR and the civilians until the beginning of the evacuation.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That brings us to the 12th of July. Would you please tell the Trial Chamber simply what you did that day, starting from the beginning.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: Well, early in the morning we headed out from the Yellow Bridge, or, in fact, we came to the Yellow Bridge, and we headed towards Potocari. To the right of the road there was the PJP unit, so the Zvornik PJP unit. To the left of the road there were members of the -- some of the members of the deserters' unit, and along the middle of the road there were some members heading towards the base in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Please continue, sir. What did you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: Well, we reached the base, and the civilians there. We stopped there, awaiting further developments. And then sometime at around approximately nine or 1000 hours, Mr. Borovcanin appeared, and so did General Mladic and they spoke, they were near a house. I was a little bit further away from them, and I don't know what they talked about and how they talked about it. After that, at one point, I don't know the exact time, I was ordered to transfer two platoons to the route from the part of Bratunac towards Konjevic Polje to secure this route, and that another platoon was to remain there because of the evacuation. At one point General Mladic showed up with his escort - I don't know what time it was - and he said, he asked in a taunting manner, it was a really ugly way of asking us, a rude manner. This is what I've already stated. He asked, "You police cunts, which one of you dares come with me to this mass of people?" So this was the way he talked to us. I took Dragan Vasiljevic with me, he was Mr. Borovcanin's driver. And I went to this mass of people together with General Mladic. General Mladic was distributing food and talking to these people. He told them to be calm, that transportation would be made available and that they would leave. So he talked to them and food was distributed to them. At one point during this distribution of food Mr. Vaso Mijovic showed up, together with his team. He was in the Serbian MUP. General Mladic took some containers of juice that he had in his jeep and he went on to distribute that to the people, to the civilians who were gathered there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Let me stop you right there, sir. You just referred to an individual and I'm not sure the transcript caught the name, first of all. Can you just restate the name, please. Who showed up together, according to the transcript, with his team.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: He was alone. He was not with his team. Vaso Mijovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And just briefly, how do you know who this individual is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: Well, in 1993 I received an order to go to Bratunac, to see what was happening there, because a unit commanded by Vaso Mijovic was stationed there. I think there was an attack on the Bratunac police station, and I was to go there and to see what the situation was like, to calm the situation, and to report back on the events. And that's how I met Mr. Vaso Mijovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And do you recall ever seeing this individual from this time in 1993 until the 12th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And you mentioned that he was not with his team. Did you see any evidence or receive any reports during your time in Potocari that there were any other members of any Serbian MUP units located there at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: You mean the Republic of Serbia MUP?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: I did not see any members of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia. I did not receive any information that there had been any in the area where I had been.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, I want to go back just a little bit, sir. You just described the distribution of some -- some juice and some other items to the crowd. Do you remember at some point that morning actually entering the UN base with a Dutch officer? And if you do, can you describe that series of events for the Trial Chamber, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: Yes, at one point Mr. Borovcanin, myself, and a member -- an officer, I don't know his exact rank, we went into the UNPROFOR base and we checked the situation there. We saw that there was a large number of civilians there, including some injured people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt you. I like to be clarified with the term "Serbian MUP." He said that he didn't see any unit, Serbian MUP unit, but earlier the witness said Vaso Mijovic is a member, he was in the Serbian MUP, and he -- a unit commanded Vaso Mijovic was stationed there, and so on. So I was not clear about that, whether he meant, when he's saying Vaso Mijovic was in the Serbian MUP, did he mean the MUP in the -- of the Republic of Serbia. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, did you understand His Honour's query?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I did understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you just clarify whether this individual was a member of the MUP of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: Well, as far as I remember, in 1993 I had information that he was a member of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could you confirm the rest, because Judge Kwon put a very important question, that when you saw him on that occasion he was alone and not with his team?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, on that occasion he was alone. No other members were with him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, would you take us from -- after the juices and some of the food stuffs are distributed to the crowd, what do you recall happening next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: Well, I think that at one point I left this location, and I went to check the route where the men were being deployed, and when I reached a flat area I saw --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Before you continue, because it's -- I want to confirm that when Mr. -- when Judge Kwon put his question he did not interrupt the sequence of your answer. At the time your question that Mr. Thayer put to you was the following: "Now, I want to go back just a little bit, sir. You just described the distribution of some juices and some other items to the crowd. Do you remember at some point that morning actually entering the UN base with a Dutch officer? And if you do, can you describe the series of events for the Trial Chamber, please." And you had started giving your answer. And what I'm going to ask you now is to continue, finish that answer. You said, "Yes, at one point Mr. Borovcanin, myself, and a member, an officer, I don't know his exact rank, we went into the UNPROFOR base and we checked the situation there. We saw that there was a large number of civilians there, including some injured people." What else did you have to say in answering that question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I said that we went into the base with this officer of the Dutch battalion to check whether there were any more civilians there and in general what was there. We saw that there were civilians in a hangar and that there were some injured people there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, you had just started telling us about travelling to the communication to which some Jahorina members had been deployed. Can you please continue with that description?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: Well, they were deployed, I don't know exactly what their starting point was, outside of Bratunac in the direction of Konjevic Polje, and the second part of the unit, I don't know when it actually arrived, was also deployed around Konjevic Polje. So they hooked up. In this period I went to visit those units at one point, and I saw that along this communication there were some dead bodies, and I saw -- when I reached a flat area, a plateau, I saw a group of civilians that had surrendered. I believe that General Mladic was there, and so was Mr. Borovcanin. I was there, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: You have described this area as being a flat area. Was it level with the ground or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: Well, as far as I remember, that was a plateau slightly raised to the right side of the road when you go from Bratunac to Konjevic Polje. So that's how I remember this.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall what, if anything, General Mladic did at the time that you were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: I think that he talked to them. He explained to them that they would be evacuated. I don't know what else he told them. At any rate, he talked to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what do you recall Mr. Borovcanin doing, if anything, while you were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: I don't remember that. I think that he was also present.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall who was securing or guarding those prisoners at that location, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: As far as I remember, I think it was the members from Jahorina and that there were also some army soldiers. I'm sure, though, that the members from Jahorina were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber what you did next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: I don't know what happened to that group of civilians who were there. I think that I went back to Potocari and after some time the evacuation of civilians started. I stood at a position in front of the UNPROFOR headquarters, instructing the buses and trucks to turn around so that the civilians could go in and out. Allegedly they were supposed to be evacuated and taken to Kladanj. That is to say, via Bratunac, Konjevic Polje, Vlasenica, Kladanj, and as far as I was informed, UNPROFOR was supposed to escort them. Whether they did it or not, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, sir, do you recall seeing any UNPROFOR soldiers boarding the buses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall ever seeing any UNPROFOR vehicles accompanying the buses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So can you describe, with some more precision, what exactly you were doing at this location in front of the UN base?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: Mr. Borovcanin tasked me with evacuating the civilians. As soon as the buses started arriving, and the trucks, since the area was quite small and there was a huge crowd of people, I attempted to ensure that the civilians were evacuated as soon as possible, to the best of my abilities. That's why I instructed the buses and trucks to turn around, because as they arrived, civilians left the crowd in which they were, and boarded the vehicles as they arrived. And then the vehicles left. I don't know much about their departure. That's the job that I was doing there. Mostly because I saw this crowd of people assembled there, and -- it was difficult for me to watch that sight, and I attempted to evacuate them as soon as possible. Three years ago I said to the investigator in Banja Luka that I had seen a group of men who had been separated. They also got into the vehicles and departed with the column. Whether they were separated from the column, when, and where, I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer, did I direct your attention to lines 2 and 3 of this page, page 65, and I'm seeking your opinion on whether that should be redacted or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I think we're -- I think we're safe with that, Your Honour, for a couple of reasons which I don't need to discuss.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. We rely on your good judgement, I mean when we ask you both you and Defence teams on this, we are relying pretty much on your judgement. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And I do appreciate the intervention, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, just to make clear, sir, you referred to a group of men who had been separated, and I just want to clarify: Did you see at any time on the 12th of July, Muslim men being separated from their families?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: I didn't, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did you receive any reports of that happening on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: I didn't, sir. However, I saw the column, and I could see that they had been separated. They were in the column, but separated. They boarded the buses and trucks separate from others.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you see any civilians abused, hit, kicked, or pushed towards or on to any of the buses on 12 July?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: (redacted) I don't like to see anybody hitting anyone else. What I don't want others to do unto me, I don't do unto them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Same thing as before. Wouldn't this identify him, at least to those who may have been present at the time?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I think we need to ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think so. So let's redact, please, line 1, page 66 to the first part of second line on page 66. Witness, we are -- Witness, we are trying to do our best to protect your identity. So when you need to give us information which would reveal your identity, even if it's to one person, ask us, draw our attention to that, and we will go into private session. All right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So in the meantime we will redact that and you may proceed, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. And if we may move into private session for this series of questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, let's move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, did you see any Muslim men directed towards or placed in any detention locations around the UN base on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you receive any reports of that happening on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: You testified a little while ago about seeing the column of men passing by the buses. Do you have any knowledge as to how those men were separated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: I don't have, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I think that it was asked and answered, and the Prosecution is trying to receive some answer which cannot be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't think that precise question was -- was asked. He indicated that he saw these individuals and I'm just following up on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, did you understand my question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: Could you please repeat it?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: You described a few moments ago, seeing men who had been separated, passing by the buses, and my question simply is: Do you have any knowledge as to how those men had been separated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: I don't have, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall having any contact or seeing Momir Nikolic on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: As far as I remember, I had no contact whatsoever with Momir Nikolic, at least I don't remember that contact.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall having any contact or conversations with any VRS members that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: Well, there were many members of the army and police there. There were many contacts. I don't know the names of the people, but there was a huge number of members, both of police and the army there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you, sir, while you were in Potocari on 12 July, can you identify for the Trial Chamber what other units or formations or detachments were there that you remember seeing, either at Potocari or passing through?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: Certain units passed through the area, military units, police units. A company of the Zvornik PJP was there, and I don't know when they left. There were various groups there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall any VRS units staying on the site of Potocari in addition to the Jahorina and PJP units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, there was a unit of the military police there. I believe that they were from the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: At this time, if we may have P01516 displayed on e-court, please. And I think when it comes up we'll have to turn it upside down, please. And if we could zoom in just a little bit, that would be helpful. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, just take a moment, if you would, and orient yourself on the image before you. And just let us know when you are comfortable that you are recognising what this is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: As far as I can see, this is the UNPROFOR unit base.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And I'm going to ask you, with the assistance of Madam Usher, to make a few markings on this. Would you please indicate first the direction towards Bratunac? And if you would do -- just please draw an arrow and a B next to the arrow.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: Well, I can't orient myself really enough to be able to tell you where Bratunac is.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Can you identify where you were directing the buses, based on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: Well, the picture is not entirely clear to me. I know that I stood right in front of the entrance to the UNPROFOR base, and this is where I turned the buses around.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you make out where the entrance to the UNPROFOR base is on this image?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: It's very hard for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Maybe what we can do, Your Honour, is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If he's finding it difficult, I mean, we can understand that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We'll -- I'll move on and perhaps come up with another idea during the break --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: -- and we'll see where we can go from there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So we can dispense with this exhibit for the time being, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Perhaps we could zoom out a little bit and perhaps that could be more helpful to the witness. Let's try that first. Does that help you more, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To tell you the truth, it's not helping me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think I -- there is an exhibit, I might be able to show in consultation with my learned friends, but I'll have to consult with them during the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you want the break now?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I think that might be helpful, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, okay. We'll have a 25-minute break starting from now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I think we have arrived at a solution to the difficulties we were encountering, and I apologise for the delay, and I thank everyone for their flexibility and understanding. What we are going to do with the Court's permission is use some exhibits that I had intended to use, but about which the Defence has been placed on notice previously. These -- this exhibit does not have a 65 ter number, but I will identify it for the record and I think we can take care of matters a little down the line. May I proceed, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, you may proceed. We hear no objections. I suppose this has been --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No objections on our side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- discussed amongst you before. Thank you, Mr. Lazarevic. Go ahead, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If we may enter private session for a moment, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Certainly. We'll just check on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session now.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, on the image that's on the ELMO, can you identify the location in which you were directing buses in Potocari on the 12th of July? Do you see that area on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: I think I can now.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And would you just -- let me hand you a pen, because we're not going to mark that actual piece of evidence right now. I'm going to have to use a black and white photograph, since this is a piece of evidence from the actual evidence room, but I -- if you would just mark the location so the Trial Chamber can see that. And then we'll mark it black and white. I'm sorry, point. Point with that pointer, the location where you were directing buses on 12 July.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: I think that's the one, here.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And there is a small dot there, sir. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. I'm going to hand you a black and white copy for the purposes of marking the exhibit here today. And would you please mark with that marker that's being handed to you the location where you were working on 12 July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you just draw a circle around that, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, having had an opportunity to look at the map a little bit, do you think you can recall well enough the paths that the Jahorina units took and the Zvornik PJP units took upon their entry into Potocari on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. I'd ask you at this point, if you could just draw arrow on that map to indicate the direction in which, first of all, the Jahorina units travelled on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if you could, can you just mark a J next to the two arrows which you have drawn on this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Can you mark the path taken by the PJP units as they entered Potocari?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if you would just write PJP next to the arrow.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, if you would continue looking at that photograph, there is a structure, it appears to be a white-coloured building. Right at the tip of the arrow you just drew marking the route of the PJP and directly across from the location which you circled, do you have any recollection, sir, of any Muslim men being taken to that location at any time on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: I don't recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, if you could just write "PW-160" anywhere on one of the corners of that document, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And I thank you. Thank you, Madam Usher. Sir, I'd like to turn your attention now to the activities along the communication, the road that runs between Bratunac and Konjevic Polje, okay?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And just to verify, are we in open session? Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And we were in open session for this last part as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That's fine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you describe for the Trial Chamber the approximate locations along that communication where the Jahorina companies were deployed? And if you can't remember exactly, that's fine, but if just generally you could describe where they were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: Well, I can't be specific about the location, but I think in the Kravica area and in the direction of Konjevic Polje and then from Konjevic Polje to Bratunac, I don't know where it was exactly that the units hooked up, but these units were deployed there in those areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you be a little bit more specific in terms of, for example, which units were deployed from the area of Konjevic Polje in the direction of Kravica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: Well, the two companies were deployed securing the communications, and there was also the Sekovici unit, the Sekovici unit, the special police brigade unit from Sekovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Let me be a little bit more specific, sir. I think previously you testified that the Jahorina units secured a particular portion of that road, and hooked up somewhere. Can you be a little bit more specific about what you mean by that? And then I'll have a couple follow-up questions.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: Well, from the Bratunac area our units were not deployed there in the exit from the town. Our units were not deployed there. I don't know the exact mileage, but I do know that they were not deployed there. Now, as to what units were deployed there, I really don't know. I don't know if this part of the communication was secured by them or what they did, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Let me ask this then, sir: Do you know which company was accommodated in the Konjevic Polje area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: That was the 2nd Company of the deserters' unit. They were in the school in Konjevic Polje. That's where they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if we may move into private session just for one question, please, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: What was your understanding, sir --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Sorry, we are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what is your recollection, sir, of approximately where those 1st company members were deployed, the ones that were based in Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: Well, they were deployed from Konjevic Polje in the direction of Bratunac, along the communication. I don't know where their starting point was, but I do know that they covered that part of the communication.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you had mentioned the area of Kravica as being what you recall as possibly being the area of the starting point for the other end. Is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: For the 1st company, yes. I don't know where their starting point was, starting position, but that would be more or less that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we may again I'm sorry, Your Honour, if we may move into private session for one question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Just to make it clear, in what direction then were the 1st Company Jahorina unit members deployed from this area of Kravica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: From Bratunac to Konjevic Polje, that was the direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And is it fair to say that your recollection is that they met somewhere roughly in the middle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: Well, yes. Now, as to where exactly they met, but it was somewhere in the middle.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: With the Court's indulgence. If we may see P02111, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I would just ask you to take a look at that image in front of you, sir. And if -- do you see the area marked Kravica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you see the area marked Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And does this map more or less depict the area as you recall it at the time? Are those the locations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: I think it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And we don't have any further use at this time, thank you, for this map. Try to save a little time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours, and to you -- to my colleague, but perhaps it would be better to cut our cross-examination short to have the witness mark on this map where this location, where the two companies met, where they linked up, the two companies that he is talking about, because that might cut short our cross-examination, if he were to do that now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you wish to put --

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I can certainly put the question to him, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, if you would take the stylus and, if you can, can you just make an X or draw an X at the location where you believe the two companies linked up.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: I think I can't really put an X where the two companies met because very roughly speaking they met somewhere in the middle. I can't put an X here, I simply don't know how I could do that, given what I now recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, sir. You testified previously, sir, about inspecting the units along that communication. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: Yes, I said that I inspected the road on the 12th, that I visited this area, and that I saw General Mladic talk to the civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. I just want to ask you first, do you recall approximately how many Jahorina members were deployed on the 12th, along that stretch of the communication?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: Well, approximately around 170, I think, if anything less than that, but this is a very rough approximation.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall whether the full 200-man contingent from Jahorina ended up going to the Potocari and Konjevic Polje-Bratunac road area on or about the 12th? Let me -- before you answer, let me just ask a better question. That was a terrible question. Sir, do you recall whether the full 200-man contingent from the Jahorina training centre was sent from the centre on or about the 11th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question? I didn't understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Sorry, that wasn't much better. Do you recall in total how many of the Jahorina training centre members went to Potocari or to the road on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: On the 12th of July two platoons went from Potocari to this road, and now as to how many platoons were deployed from the 2nd company commanded by (redacted) I couldn't tell you that, I don't know. I could just make some assumptions, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if would he could just have a redaction at page 81, line 19, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's do that. Just redact the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And let's proceed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And as you travelled along this communication on the 12th of July, can you describe for the Court how the men physically were deployed on the communication?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: Well, the distance was predetermined, but I don't know what it was. I don't know whether we were supposed to keep in -- keep visual contact at all times, but at any rate, there was a certain distance that was set. I think that's how they were deployed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when you refer to a certain distance, you are referring to a certain distance between individual members of the unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: -- were these members physically on the road or were they off to the side in -- in the field?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: I think they were physically on the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, other than seeing the Jahorina members guarding the prisoners at that plateau you testified before, do you recall receiving any reports of Muslim men surrendering to Jahorina units along the road on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: I didn't have any information of them surrendering. I know about this, but I don't remember any such information.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If we may go into private session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's do that.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall what you did after you travelled along the communication?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: Well, I went down this communication, I checked -- this position of the personnel, so the one thing that I remember is that I actually went along this communication.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did you return to Potocari at that time or somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: I don't remember, but I think that I did go back to Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall what time, approximately, the transportations ended that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: Well, I don't really know. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you remember whether it was in the afternoon versus the evening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: You mean the transportations from Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: I think that on the 12th it was in the evening. I think it was actually already well into the night. Maybe 2200 hours, 2300 hours. It was in night -- it was night-time, well into the night-time.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And let me ask you this, sir: This -- this incident where you observed General Mladic addressing the group of prisoners along the communication, how certain are you that that occurred on the 12th as opposed to another day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: I think I can be sure that it was on the 12th, as far as I can remember. Well, I can get my dates mixed up, but I am telling you about what I saw, about what I know, but it is possible that I may be wrong about some dates. I can even be wrong about the time and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. After the transportation of the civilians out of Potocari ended on the 12th, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: Well, when we finished with that part of the evacuation on the 12th, we went back with the part of the unit from Potocari to the village where we were billeted. I reported to Mr. Borovcanin, and he told me to get some rest and that in the morning we would continue with the evacuation. So I went to my quarters in the school, I slept, and then the next morning I don't know the exact time, we went back to continue evacuating the civilians. And then in the morning I think that Mr. Borovcanin called me. He wanted us to meet in Bratunac, and I don't know if we had breakfast, we sat down and we talked and there was a reporter present, I don't know what newspaper he was with. I don't remember now, I'm trying to recall, but I think that after Bratunac I went back to Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Before we get to breakfast on the 13th, let me just ask you a couple more questions about the night of the 12th, all right? You mentioned that you reported to Mr. Borovcanin. Do you recall where you did that, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: Well, I think it was in the public security station in Bratunac. There was an office there. That's where we met after the 12th in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And other than giving you the order to continue the transportation the next day, did Mr. Borovcanin give you any specific orders with respect to the units along the road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: As far as I recall, I don't think so. I simply don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, were there any Jahorina members left in Potocari on the night of the -- July 12th, or did the entire contingent return to the accommodations in Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: On the 12th at night, the night between the 12th and 13th, there were no members of the deserters' unit in Potocari. They had gone back to their accommodations in Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, seeing as how you spent the night of the 12th of July near Bratunac and seeing as how you had reported to Mr. Borovcanin sometime during the evening of the 12th, did you become aware at any time of any prisoners being detained in Bratunac on the night of the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Back to the morning of the 13th, sir. After meeting Mr. Borovcanin and the reporter in Bratunac, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: As far as I remember, I went to Potocari, but to tell you the truth, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you have any recollection of being in Potocari on the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: I don't remember, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, how many days the transportations of the civilians from Potocari lasted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: As far as I remember, it took place on the 12th and 13th.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall during your interview with the OTP and during your testimony in the Blagojevic case, being asked specific questions about your activities on the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160
utterances.text: I don't remember, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: With the Court's indulgence. Your Honours, I think we'll have to go into private session, because I believe I will need to identify certain portions of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: -- transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 12th day of March, 2007, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.47 p.m.,
